name: CLIP
summary: CLIP trained image and text encoders contrastively on 400M web pairs, producing a shared embedding where arbitrary language can retrieve or classify visual content zero-shot. For manipulation this was the unlock for open-vocabulary object grounding: a robot could suddenly be told to pick up a noun it had never seen in robot data, and the perception stack would still find it.
innovation: Contrastive image-text pretraining at web scale, yielding zero-shot transfer to unseen categories.
A reusable joint embedding that downstream systems could condition on with no fine-tuning.
matters: The visual-semantic substrate under SayCan, VoxPoser and most VLA vision encoders.
limits: Weak at spatial relations, counting and fine-grained geometry, which is exactly what manipulation needs.
lineage: Transformer encoders trained contrastively; the semantic half of nearly every robot perception stack.
